thesis: Billing converts a billable business event into a customer charge and usually a financial posting. Diagnose the first wrong decision, not only the final invoice.

runtime.question: Why is the item billable now?
Which business object and quantity are being billed?
How does the source become billing state?
Which billable items may share one billing header?
Which commercial values are copied or redetermined?
What billing document now represents the charge?
What financial posting should be created?
How is the invoice communicated externally?
Should we cancel, credit, debit, or rebill?

controls.label: Copying Control
controls.owns: source-to-target requirements, data transfer, quantity basis, pricing type

controls.label: Split / Convergence
controls.owns: which items may share one billing header

controls.label: Pricing Transfer / Redetermination
controls.owns: how billing receives or recalculates price elements

controls.label: Revenue Account Determination
controls.owns: G/L account selection at FI transfer

boundaries.rule: Upstream owns the billable event; Billing owns conversion into the customer charge.
Pricing owns calculation logic; Billing owns whether pricing is copied or redetermined.
Tax owns tax logic; Billing carries the result and may change the runtime context.
Billing owns commercial values; FI owns accounting state after transfer.
Billing is the source document; external formatting, transmission and legal status remain separate responsibilities.

correction_paths.use_when: The original billing event itself must be reversed and recreated.
The customer receivable must be reduced through a controlled adjustment.
The customer receivable must be increased through a controlled adjustment.

failure_modes.symptom: Invoice quantity or source relationship is wrong.
Invoice value differs from expected sales value.
Invoice exists but FI transfer is blocked or account assignment is wrong.
Billing/FI are correct but customer or authority invoice state is wrong.
Correction fixes the amount but leaves an unclear audit trail.

what_i_ask_first: Which layer is wrong: due state, reference, split, value, FI, or external issue?
Which document owns the first incorrect value?
lead_lens.main_trade_off: Efficient billing without losing legal, accounting, and document-flow traceability.
lead_lens.typical_failure: Repairing the final invoice instead of tracing the first wrong input or ownership boundary.

assessment_prompts: A complete delivery does not appear in the billing due list. Build a hypothesis tree.
Two deliveries for one customer create two invoices. Prove the split reason before changing configuration.
The order value is 100 and the invoice is 105. Explain when this can be expected and what you inspect first.
The invoice value is correct but revenue posts to the wrong G/L. Separate pricing from account determination.
Billing and FI are correct but the e-invoice is rejected. Define ownership and recovery.
Compare cancellation/rebill with credit/debit correction after an invoice error.
